titulo: The five questions everyone asks you
subtitulo: They are always the same five — which means you can have the answers ready and spend the moment listening instead of translating
cena: A stranger has decided to talk to you, the first question landed, and you are three seconds from the polite nod that ends it.
frasePiso: The questions repeat. Prepare five answers once and every conversation after that starts on the second sentence.
decisao: ficar na conversa com cinco respostas prontas em vez de sair dela com um sorriso educado toda vez que alguém puxa assunto

steps.pt: Nearly every conversation you have in Italy opens with the same five questions. That is not a limitation — it is a script you can learn.

steps.acao: Answer with the city, not the country, if the city is one they will know.

steps.promptPt: Answer question one. Give a place they can picture. Speak now.
steps.es: Siamo di Boston, negli Stati Uniti.
steps.pinyin: SYA-mo dee BOS-ton, NE-lyee STA-tee oo-NEE-tee
steps.pt: We're from Boston, in the United States.
steps.tts: Siamo di Boston, negli Stati Uniti.

steps.pt: Question two is always how long. Give the number and the unit, the same way you did at the border.

steps.promptPt: Say how long you are staying, and add where you go next. Speak now.
steps.es: Dieci giorni. Poi andiamo in Sicilia.
steps.pinyin: dee-EH-chee JOR-nee. poy an-DYA-mo een see-CHEE-lya
steps.pt: Ten days. Then we're going to Sicily.
steps.tts: Dieci giorni. Poi andiamo in Sicilia.

steps.es: È la prima volta in Italia?
steps.pt: Is this your first time in Italy?
steps.tts: È la prima volta in Italia?

steps.promptPt: Answer question three and give them something to react to. Speak now.
steps.es: No, la seconda. La prima volta ero a Roma.
steps.pinyin: no, la se-KON-da. la PREE-ma VOL-ta EH-ro a RO-ma
steps.pt: No, the second. The first time I was in Rome.
steps.tts: No, la seconda. La prima volta ero a Roma.

steps.pt: Question four is what you do. Two words is a complete answer — nobody is asking for your career.

steps.promptPt: Say what you do, briefly. Speak now.

steps.pt: Question five is the one that matters: do you like it here. The frame is mi piace plus the thing, and a specific answer opens the conversation.

steps.promptPt: Say what you like, naming one concrete thing. Speak now.
steps.es: Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati.
steps.pinyin: mee PYA-che tan-TEES-see-mo, so-prat-TOOT-to ee mer-KA-tee
steps.pt: I like it enormously, the markets above all.
steps.tts: Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati.

steps.acao: This is the payoff. Say yes and write down what they name.
steps.es: Allora domani deve andare a quello di Sant'Ambrogio. Meno turisti.
steps.pt: Then tomorrow you have to go to the Sant'Ambrogio one. Fewer tourists.
steps.tts: Allora domani deve andare a quello di Sant'Ambrogio. Meno turisti.

steps.promptPt: Turn it around — ask them the question they asked you. Speak now.
You lost the question entirely. Stay in the conversation instead of leaving it. Speak now.
steps.es: Scusi, mi sono perso. Può ripetere?
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, mee SO-no PER-so. pwoh ree-PE-te-re
steps.pt: Sorry, I lost you. Can you repeat that?
steps.tts: Scusi, mi sono perso. Può ripetere?

steps.promptPt: You have to go, and you want the door left open. Speak now.
steps.es: È stato un piacere. Magari ci vediamo domani.
steps.pinyin: eh STA-to oon pya-CHE-re. ma-GA-ree chee ve-DYA-mo do-MA-nee
steps.pt: It's been a pleasure. Maybe we'll see each other tomorrow.
steps.tts: È stato un piacere. Magari ci vediamo domani.

steps.es: Siamo di Boston. Dieci giorni. Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati. E lei è di qui?
steps.pinyin: SYA-mo dee BOS-ton. dee-EH-chee JOR-nee. mee PYA-che tan-TEES-see-mo so-prat-TOOT-to ee mer-KA-tee. eh lay eh dee kwee
steps.pt: Shadow the four answers and the question that hands it back.
steps.tts: Siamo di Boston. Dieci giorni. Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati. E lei è di qui?

steps.pt: I05 done. Where from, how long, first time, what you do, do you like it — and then one question back.

secoes.corpo: Write your five answers before the trip and say them out loud twice. The gain is not the sentences — it is that you spend the actual conversation listening instead of assembling.

exemplos.es: Siamo di Boston, negli Stati Uniti.
exemplos.pt: We're from Boston, in the United States.

secoes.corpo: Mi piace tutto ends the exchange. Naming one thing you liked gives the other person something to improve on, and what comes back is usually the version locals actually use.

secoes.titulo: The question back is the whole trick
secoes.corpo: E lei è di qui? converts an interview into a conversation. Italians ask a lot of questions and expect them returned; not returning one reads as not being interested.
Lei is the polite form and is safe with anyone older, anyone working, and anyone you have just met. If they switch to tu, follow them. You are never wrong for having started with lei.

permissao: You are allowed to stay in a conversation you are only half following. Saying mi sono perso and asking for a repeat is what people who speak the language do — leaving with a polite smile because catching up felt like too much work is the only version of this that costs you something.
espelho: Anyone who has nodded through the end of a phone call they stopped following knows this exact exit. The instinct to escape rather than admit you lost the thread is not about foreign languages — it just gets more expensive in one.

fichasCulturais.sinal: A stranger asks you several personal-sounding questions in a row — where you're from, what you do, whether you're married — within two minutes of meeting.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This is intrusive, and I am being interrogated.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: These questions are the standard opening moves of Italian small talk, closer to establishing who you both are than to gathering information. Not asking them can read as coldness rather than as respect for privacy.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer short and true, then return one of the same questions. That is the expected shape of the exchange.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get past the opening in thirty seconds and into the part where they tell you which market to go to, which is where the value of the conversation actually is.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a licence for the same volley from you towards someone visibly working through a queue, and not an obligation to answer anything you would rather not — deflecting one question warmly does not break the exchange.
